description: How much credit support will NVIDIA have committed to AI cloud partners for their NVIDIA-powered compute infrastructure, and how large is the resulting guarantee/credit exposure?
outcome: The outstanding amount of credit support, guarantees or backstop NVIDIA has extended to AI cloud partners under its new revenue-sharing and credit-support model, disclosed at its next annual report.
period: Next annual report (Form 10-K for the fiscal year ending late January 2027, likely filed early 2027): the outstanding amount of credit support/guarantees; set by the reason (obligation already undertaken, tracked at the next annual report).

description: Will NVIDIA sign a financial guarantee/backstop for OpenAI's lease of a large data center in Ohio — and at what amount — large enough to change NVIDIA's credit risk?
outcome: Whether NVIDIA executes (signs) a guarantee or capacity/lease backstop for OpenAI's Ohio data-center lease, and the resulting amount, by the check date.
period: Check date of 31 December 2027 (18 months from the 1 July 2026 item date): whether the guarantee is signed by then; set by the rule for an unsigned obligation (a check date within 18 months of the item).

description: Will NVIDIA's next-generation Vera Rubin AI chip platform begin first shipments — the step that brings revenue — before the end of calendar 2026?
outcome: Whether Vera Rubin reaches first shipments (start of revenue) by the end of 2026.
period: End of calendar 2026, the date the item supports ('could begin shipping later this year' relative to its 2 July 2026 date).

description: Will the combined data center capital expenditure of the big four AI hyperscalers reach $1 trillion in calendar 2027, the aggregate AI-infrastructure spend Nvidia projects and on which its GPU demand depends?
outcome: The big four AI hyperscalers' combined data center capital expenditure for calendar 2027, as disclosed in their full-year results.
period: Calendar 2027 (the item's 'next year' from its 2026 date), when the four hyperscalers report full-year capex; set by the item, which projects the figure could reach $1 trillion in 2027 up from around $650 billion in 2026.

description: What will contract prices for AI memory (LPDDR5X, HBM, 3D NAND/DRAM) be through calendar 2026-2027 — the input that now makes up roughly 25-30% of Nvidia's Vera Rubin rack cost?
outcome: The level and direction of contract memory (DRAM, NAND, HBM) prices in 2026-2027 and the resulting per-rack memory content cost (about $2 million on the VR200).
period: Calendar 2026-2027 memory contract cycles; set by the item's forward cost period (second half of 2026 and beyond).

description: Will NVIDIA's Rubin Ultra rack-scale platform — the Kyber NVL144 architecture that houses 144 Rubin Ultra GPUs — reach first shipments in 2027 as originally planned, or slip to 2028 as SemiAnalysis reports?
outcome: Whether NVIDIA's Kyber NVL144 / Rubin Ultra rack platform reaches first shipments (the step that brings revenue) in 2027 or is delayed to 2028.
period: 2028 — the release date SemiAnalysis reports Kyber has been pushed to from an original 2027; the question is settled when Kyber NVL144 / Rubin Ultra first ships (the item supports the original-2027-vs-2028 timing).

description: What will the outstanding amount of NVIDIA's supply (purchase) commitments to suppliers be at its next annual report — the obligations that lock it into buying capacity and services for its AI systems?
outcome: The outstanding supply/purchase commitments disclosed in NVIDIA's next annual report, compared with the $119 billion cited in this item.
period: Next annual report (Form 10-K for the fiscal year ending late January 2027, likely filed early 2027); set by the reason — an obligation already undertaken is tracked by its amount at the next annual report.

description: How much revenue will the big four hyperscalers' in-house AI accelerators (Amazon Trainium, Google TPU, Microsoft Maia, Meta MTIA) generate in calendar 2026 — the combined custom-silicon quantity competing with NVIDIA GPUs, whose customers also fund NVIDIA's data center segment?
outcome: The combined calendar-2026 revenue (or disclosed shipment volume) of the four hyperscalers' in-house AI accelerator programmes, as disclosed in their full-year 2026 results and earnings calls.
period: Calendar 2026, measured at the hyperscalers' full-year 2026 disclosures (early 2027); next/current calendar year set by the item's 6 July 2026 date and by the rule that a shared quantity takes its release date.

description: What share of Chinese enterprises' AI accelerator budget will be allocated to domestic (Chinese-made) products versus Nvidia over the 12 months following the July 2026 survey, and will it rise toward the 46% executives indicated from 30% today?
outcome: The share of surveyed Chinese enterprise AI accelerator budget going to domestic products — and by implication Nvidia's remaining share — over the 12 months after the July 2026 survey.
period: The 12 months from the Jul 7 2026 Bloomberg Intelligence survey (roughly H2 2026 – H1 2027); set by the survey's 'next 12 months' horizon, checked against a follow-up survey.

description: Will the U.S. government (Congress and/or the FCC) enact legislation or regulation to ban or phase out Chinese-made lidar sensors in U.S. autonomous/robotics systems, which would change the sensor options and cost competitiveness available to NVIDIA's DRIVE Hyperion autonomous-vehicle platform?
outcome: Whether proposed U.S. legislation/regulation to phase out Chinese-made lidar technology in the United States is enacted (and its scope and timing).
period: Pending regulatory/legislative decision — checked at NVIDIA's current fiscal year-end (fiscal year ending late January 2027), per the rule that a pending regulatory decision is tracked to the current fiscal year-end.

description: Will China's government approve imports of Nvidia's H200 AI chips into China — and roughly how many — enabling Nvidia to begin generating H200 revenue in the country?
outcome: Whether Chinese authorities grant approval for Alibaba, ByteDance, DeepSeek and other firms to import Nvidia H200 chips (potentially a total below 200,000), as reflected in official Chinese government decisions and in Nvidia's disclosed China H200 revenue.
period: Nvidia's current fiscal year-end (fiscal year ending late January 2027), checked at its next annual report/10-K; set by the rule that a pending regulatory decision is tracked to the current fiscal year-end.

description: Will France's competition authority (Autorité de la concurrence) conclude its antitrust investigation into Nvidia's cloud-AI and GPU-market practices by the check date, and will it impose remedies or fines?
outcome: The French competition authority's conclusion of its antitrust investigation into alleged anti-competitive practices in the cloud-AI and GPU markets, and any remedies or fines imposed.
period: Nvidia's current fiscal year-end (fiscal year ending late January 2027); set by the rule that a pending regulatory decision is tracked to the current fiscal year-end.
